comparisons.peer_topic: Level 3 Financial Instrument Gains and Losses Details
comparisons.peer_summary: Gains and losses in earnings are reported across various line items including trading accounts, derivatives, and MSRs, while OCI includes unrealized gains/losses on AFS securities and credit spread changes on long-term debt, with specific net unrealized loss amounts provided for held instruments.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC report net realized and unrealized gains/losses for Level 3 instruments, but the composition differs significantly. GS reports a net loss of $104 million on Level 3 derivatives, with gains driven by commodity and interest rate derivatives offset by equity derivative losses. In contrast, BAC discloses net unrealized losses of $104 million specifically for Level 3 financial instruments still held, attributing these to broader categories like trading accounts and MSRs, without breaking down the gain/loss drivers by specific derivative asset class (commodity vs equity) to the same extent as GS.

sentences.text: The net realized and unrealized losses on level 3 derivatives of $104 million (reflecting $129 million of net realized losses and $25 million of net unrealized gains) for 2024 included gains/(losses) of $(115) million reported in market making and $11 million reported in other principal transactions.

The net unrealized gains on level 3 derivatives for 2024 primarily reflected gains on certain commodity derivatives (principally due to the impact of changes in commodity prices) and gains on certain interest rate derivatives (principally due to an increase in interest rates), partially offset by losses on certain equity derivatives (principally due to the impact of changes in equity prices).
Amounts include net unrealized losses of $104 million and $324 million related to financial instruments still held at December 31, 2024 and 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment for Level 3 gains, losses, and securities valuation changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Net realized/unrealized gains and losses for Level 3 assets and liabilities are presented as increases or decreases to those positions. Changes in fair value of available-for-sale debt securities are recorded in AOCI (unless credit impairment), while sales gains/losses go to the Consolidated Statement of Income; unrealized gains/losses on MSRs are recorded in Other revenue.
comparisons.comparison: While GS explicitly quantifies the $104 million net loss on Level 3 derivatives, Citi's Level 3 disclosure focuses on the accounting treatment for gains and losses rather than providing a specific aggregate dollar amount for derivative losses in the same summary context. Citi states that net realized/unrealized gains/losses are presented as increases/decreases to Level 3 assets/liabilities and notes that unrealized gains/losses on MSRs are recorded in Other revenue, whereas GS attributes its gains/losses primarily to market making and other principal transactions.

sentences.text: The net realized and unrealized losses on level 3 derivatives of $104 million (reflecting $129 million of net realized losses and $25 million of net unrealized gains) for 2024 included gains/(losses) of $(115) million reported in market making and $11 million reported in other principal transactions.
(1)Net realized/unrealized gains (losses) are presented as increase (decrease) to Level 3 assets, and as (increase) decrease to Level 3 liabilities.
(2)Unrealized gains (losses) on MSRs are recorded in Other revenue in the Consolidated Statement of Income.

comparisons.peer_topic: Reporting and Classification Details for Level 3 Instruments
comparisons.peer_summary: Level 3 derivatives are presented on a net basis. Realized and unrealized gains/losses on Level 3 AFS securities were not material for 2024-2022, with unrealized gains/losses due to DVA for fair value option elected liabilities reported in OCI as $(50) million, $(158) million, and $(529) million respectively. Other items include changes in fair value for MSRs in mortgage fees, DVA in principal transactions revenue, loan originations included in purchases, and maturities/repayments.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose gains/losses associated with Level 3 instruments, but the materiality and composition differ. GS reports a significant $104 million net loss on Level 3 derivatives, driven by specific market factors. JPM, conversely, states that realized and unrealized gains/losses on Level 3 AFS securities were not material for 2024, and highlights that unrealized losses due to DVA (debit valuation adjustment) for fair value option elected liabilities were reported in OCI, showing a different primary driver for their Level 3 fair value changes.

sentences.text: The net realized and unrealized losses on level 3 derivatives of $104 million (reflecting $129 million of net realized losses and $25 million of net unrealized gains) for 2024 included gains/(losses) of $(115) million reported in market making and $11 million reported in other principal transactions.
Realized and unrealized gains/(losses) recorded on level 3 AFS securities were not material for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022.
Unrealized (gains)/losses are reported in OCI, and were $(50) million, $(158) million and $(529) million for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively.

comparisons.peer_topic: Level 3 hedge interaction and revenue inclusion
comparisons.peer_summary: Realized and unrealized gains/losses for Level 3 items do not reflect related gains/losses on hedging instruments in Level 1 or 2, and total gains/losses are primarily included in Trading revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley disclose gains/losses for Level 3 instruments reported in income statement line items. GS reports a net loss of $104 million on Level 3 derivatives included in market making and other principal transactions. MS similarly reports that total realized and unrealized gains/losses for Level 3 items are primarily included in Trading revenues, but explicitly notes that these reported figures do not reflect related gains/losses on hedging instruments in Level 1 or 2, a nuance not emphasized in GS's derivative rollforward summary.

The realized and unrealized gains or losses for assets and liabilities within the Level 3 category presented in the previous tables do not reflect the related realized and unrealized gains or losses on hedging instruments that have been classified by the Firm within the Level 1 and/or Level 2 categories.
